title: Revenue report (GET /reports/:reportId)
description: How an admin fetches a revenue summary (`daily` or `monthly`), from the request through the config lookup to the SELECT ... FROM ${tableName} statement flagged by Semgrep (src/repositories/reportRepository.js:8).

steps.title: Client: HTTP request
description: **What happens:** an admin asks for a named report. The only input is the path segment `reportId`.
| No `Authorization` header, or not `Bearer …` | 401 | `{"error":"missing token"}` | captured |
| Token not in `users.api_token` | 401 | `{"error":"invalid token"}` | derived from code, not run |
| Valid token, role is not `admin` (alice, bob) | 403 | `{"error":"forbidden"}` | derived from code, not run |
| `reportId` not a key of `config/reports.js` | 404 | `{"error":"unknown report"}` | derived from code, not run |
| `reportId` is an inherited object key (`constructor`, `toString`) | 500 | `{"error":"internal error"}` | derived from code, not run |
| Success | 200 | `{"title":…,"orders":n,"revenue":"…"}` | derived from code, not run |
**Next →** Express matches the path against the mounted routers (step 2).

steps.title: App: mount reports router
description: **What happens:** after the body parsers and the orders router, the reports router is mounted at the root.

steps.title: Routing: GET /reports/:reportId
description: **What happens:** two middlewares run before the controller: authentication, then a role check for `admin`. `:reportId` captures one path segment (URL-decoded) into `req.params.reportId`.

steps.title: Auth: read Bearer token
description: **What happens:** same middleware as the orders flow. A missing header or another scheme stops the request (captured from the running app):

steps.title: Auth: authenticate token
description: **What happens:** an unknown token stops the request; otherwise `req.user` is set.

steps.title: Auth store: token lookup
steps.pattern: ('SELECT id, username, role FROM users WHERE api_token = \$1', \[token\])
description: **What happens:** parameterised lookup of the token; returns the user's `role`, used by the next step.
req.user = { id: 3, username: 'admin', role: 'admin' }   // for tok_admin_c41f6e

steps.title: Authz: require admin role
description: **What happens:** only users whose `role` column is `admin` continue. alice and bob (role `user`) are stopped:

steps.title: Controller: look up reportId
description: **What happens:** the path value is used only as a key into the report definitions in `config/reports.js`; the client never sends a table name.
// → { title: 'Orders in the last 24 hours', table: 'orders_daily_summary' }

steps.title: Config: report definitions
description: **What happens:** a hard-coded map of two reports, each with a fixed `table` (a view defined in `db/init.sql`). These two strings are the only table names defined here.
**Security:** the map is a plain object literal, so inherited keys (`constructor`, `toString`, `__proto__`) are also found by the lookup in step 8; their `.table` is `undefined`.

steps.title: Controller: unknown report → 404
description: **What happens:** a `reportId` that is not a key of the map stops the request:

steps.title: Service: pass definition.table
description: **What happens:** the service passes the configured table name to the repository, where it is called `tableName`.

steps.title: Store: FROM interpolation
description: **What happens:** `tableName` is written into the SQL text with a template literal. This is the line Semgrep flagged (`reportRepository.js:8`). There are no bound parameters.
SELECT count(*)::int AS orders, coalesce(sum(total), 0) AS revenue FROM orders_daily_summary
**Security:** the value here always comes from `config/reports.js` (steps 8–11), not from the request text; for an inherited key it is `undefined`, giving `FROM undefined`.

steps.title: Postgres: aggregate the view
description: **What happens:** Postgres counts and sums the rows of the view. With `FROM undefined` it fails with `relation "undefined" does not exist`, which rejects the promise.
**Next →** the service merges the result (step 14) or the error handler runs (step 16).

steps.title: Service: add the title
description: **What happens:** combines the configured title with the aggregate row.

steps.title: Response: 200 JSON
description: **What happens:** the report is returned as JSON. With the seed data loaded just now, orders 1 (42.50) and 4 (310.00) are in the last 24 hours; `revenue` is a string because `pg` returns `NUMERIC` as text:
(derived from code and db/init.sql, not run)
